body.text: In this reviewed 119th-Congress sample, Foushee supported reporting and evidence, research, or implementation conditions in two independent episodes, while opposing three specific proposals concerning retired-service firearm access, broader D.C. police pursuit authority, and repeal of most reviewed D.C. policing restrictions.

heading.text: Certification, fentanyl research provisions, and officer-safety reporting

body.text: Across independent episodes, Foushee supported an overdose-reduction certification condition, a later fentanyl framework with research provisions, and officer-safety reporting requirements.

heading.text: Retired-service firearm access, D.C. pursuit authority, and policing-rule rollbacks

body.text: Across independent episodes, Foushee opposed creating a reviewed federal program for eligible current and retired officers to buy qualifying retired agency firearms, broader D.C. police pursuit authority, and repeal of most reviewed D.C. policing restrictions.

Within one fentanyl legislative episode, Foushee supported a certification amendment, opposed the earlier House bill, and supported a later related framework that permanently scheduled fentanyl-related substances and included research provisions. These related stages count as one episode for breadth and do not establish a change in position, motive, or philosophy.

review_limitations.text: Seven substantive actions across five independent episodes are a bounded 119th-Congress sample, not the complete Justice record.
The D.C. pursuit proposal included risk, futility, and alternative-apprehension exceptions.
The D.C. reform-repeal substitute retained the neck-restraint and vehicular-pursuit subtitles.
The later fentanyl framework combined permanent scheduling and enforcement consequences with research provisions.
The three related fentanyl actions form one mixed episode and do not establish a change in position, motive, or philosophy.
The reviewed H.R. 2240 official argument evidence was one-sided; no opposing argument was synthesized.
The retired-firearm action does not establish a general position on police tools or police equipment.
